description: Reviewer reported that their vehicle went missing after being parked improperly near a yellow line.

review_text:
So yesterday we had this weird experience.. if you are new to Bangalore & if you are visiting commercial street for the 1st time, be careful while parking your vehicle. There might be a yellow line on the footpath. It means from there you shouldn't park your vehicle. If you don't take care, by the time you come back from your shopping, your vehicle will be missing. You don't even know where your vehicle is. You won't even have a contact number written to contact for.

We asked local shop people, they answered it in a very cool way asking us to go to CSE hospital. This very same people won't even warn you while you are parking without knowing this ritual. Or sometimes they may say it's ok to park there. But beware.. So when we tried to catch an auto and said CSE hospital, he immediately asked "is your vehicle missing?" So it's a common thing for them. He confidently said that he would take to some other place where we can find our vehicle. There you might be fined Rs.1650/-. Autowala will teach you how to talk to them. Better rush before 8:30pm to take your vehicle.

So our autowala suggested us to park our vehicle from next time at any mall nearby.

Be careful guys..

& about shopping, we can shop at low prices. Good place for shopping ..

review_text: Redevelopment or Public Harassment? South Western Railway needs to answer.For over six months, passengers at the metro-connected railway station have been facing hazardous conditions under the guise of "construction".How can a major transit hub lack digital display boards on its main Foot Over Bridges? title: Poor lighting and confusing entry signage
location: Tumkur Rd, Dr.Ambedkar Nagar, Yeswanthpur, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560022, India (13.023750, 77.551712)
description: Reviewer reported poor pedestrian accessibility, confusing entry signage, and unlit entry roads.
address: Tumkur Rd, Dr.Ambedkar Nagar, Yeswanthpur, Bengaluru, Karnataka 560022, India
review_text:
1. Poorly accessible for pedestrians who come by bus or auto with luggage and want to cross road; The u-turn is way far off and a 10-15 min time-waster with no pedestrian access to cross road to get to station quickly given the horrible traffic.
2. Poor signage on how to enter to the station - absolutely confusing if you dont come by metro. Which road should you enter to get to the station? Where is the station entry signage after you are dropped off? And it is not even lit!
3. Within station, FOB is far off; station signages about the platforms are not clearly visible - but if you get down the platform number could barely be seen (e,g try which side is platform 4 /5 once you get down).
4. And, the FOB once you find is at an end you have to go, climb, get down and again cross the entire train...
The renovation wont solve the pedestrian access issues from outside...so best avoid getting in from there..KR puram is better accessible IMO.
